builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Weight Space Programming for Vision Language Model Repair
summary: The technique replaces gradient-based retraining or checkpoint rollback for repairing corrupted model weights with a coding agent that edits the weight tensors directly. It costs only an agent session with API or local inference access plus the baseline weights for verification, so it fits constrained infrastructure, but it adds a fragile manual diagnostic loop rather than a reliable automated procedure. It fails when faults leave no detectable trace: after rounding away 32-bit residue in the low bits of 16-bit weights, unaided repair largely collapses, row or column permutations are never found within budget, and noise faults go undetected on the larger model.
rationale: The paper's own central result is that gradient-free agent repair of damaged weights succeeds mainly by exploiting numerical artifacts that real production failures need not leave, so it is not yet a dependable recovery practice for a constrained-infrastructure team.
technique: Agent-driven gradient-free weight repair of VLMs

claims.statement: The technique replaces gradient-based retraining or checkpoint rollback for repairing corrupted model weights with a coding agent that edits the weight tensors directly. It costs only an agent session with API or local inference access plus the baseline weights for verification, so it fits constrained infrastructure, but it adds a fragile manual diagnostic loop rather than a reliable automated procedure. It fails when faults leave no detectable trace: after rounding away 32-bit residue in the low bits of 16-bit weights, unaided repair largely collapses, row or column permutations are never found within budget, and noise faults go undetected on the larger model.

On LFM2-VL, agent repair recovered about 17 accuracy points when fault traces remained in 16-bit low bits, versus only about 4 points after those bits were rounded away; on SmolVLM unaided repair succeeded only when the prompt named a diagnostic statistic.
